summary: Scoped a follow-up to the completed 20260817-small-model-coding-agents research task. Focus is narrowed to whether any current/emerging technique raises the complexity ceiling for small models (multi-turn/long-horizon tasks) rather than compensating within it. Prioritizes the prior research's thin architectural/system-level category (context management, memory, sandboxed execution loops), recent work targeting multi-turn/long-horizon collapse specifically, direct evidence on fundamental-limit-vs-solvable-gap, and genuinely novel technique categories beyond RAG/verifiers/orchestration/distillation. Explicitly excludes re-covering the prior research's established findings (multi-turn collapse itself, benchmark-gap-widens-with-realism, verifier mechanism split) and out-of-scope efficiency/single-turn work.
